name: Voices Before Print
description: Epics, hymns and scriptures from Mesopotamia, India, China, Greece and Arabia, composed to be recited and passed on long before the printing press.

checkpoints.name: The first stories
checkpoints.note: The oldest known stories come from clay tablets in Mesopotamia and from Vedic hymns in India, kept alive by memory and by priests.

checkpoints.name: The age of epics
checkpoints.note: Greek singers, Indian poets and Chinese sages created works that became the base of their cultures: Homer's wars, the great Indian epics and the sayings of Confucius and Laozi.

checkpoints.name: The classical world
checkpoints.note: Scrolls spread across empires. Rome's poets imitated Greece, and Jewish scribes by the Dead Sea copied the texts that would form scripture.

checkpoints.name: Faith and courts
checkpoints.note: Sanskrit drama, the Quran, Arabian tales and Old English verse show how writing carried both faith and entertainment across Asia, Arabia and Europe.

checkpoints.name: Manuscripts to print
checkpoints.note: Persian and Japanese courts produced their great classics by hand, in the Americas Maya stories were written down, and in Mainz a printer made the first great printed book.
